Sana — thanks for the clear ask and the telemetry. Quick read-through and initial thoughts below; Ben and Kim will add pricing and SLA/quant specifics.

Short answers up front:
- Packaging: pilot = time-limited credits + conservative quant (FP16 or 8-bit) + cache enabled; starter = modest commit, standard quant (8-bit with selective float fallbacks), cache + batch tuning; scale = larger commit, aggressive quant profiles (int4 in supported ops), dedicated KV caching and prewarm pools.
- Batching vs cache: cache-first reduces per-token work for repeat prefixes (best for chat/assistant flows). Batching helps throughput on high-concurrency short responses. For your telemetry (long-tail + spikes) we recommend cache-first where prefix reuse is >10% and conservative batching with adaptive windows during spikes.
- Quantization: start with 8-bit quantization and run a small quality eval set from your prompts. If errors are within your tolerance, test int4 on a holding environment with A/B evaluation. We'll provide an eval checklist.

Action items from Redwood:
1) Ben: pricing sketch for 3-month pilot vs 12-month commit.
2) Kim: quantization guardrails, rollback plan, and minimal SLA asks for pilot.
3) Me: an MLP (mutual action plan) for procurement + sample eval checklist (I'll attach both).

I attached a short deck with recommended starter configs. Ben/Kim — please add specifics in thread.

Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit — quantization guardrails and SLA notes

Sana — quick technical guardrails from our applied ML team:

- Start conservative: run FP16 baseline -> 8-bit quant -> selective int4 on non-attention matmuls. For many open 30B models we've seen <2% NLL change with 8-bit; int4 can introduce artifacts and needs prompt-tuned fallback rules.
- Eval plan: we recommend a 500-prompt eval set (mix of short/long, high-entropy prompts). We provide a script to compute perplexity, token-level edit distance, and human-pass/fail sampling.
- Cache strategy: enable KV cache for sessionized traffic, set prefix TTL to 24–72 hours depending on reuse. For long-tail generation, increase soft-fallthrough to skip cache on low prefix reuse and rely on batching.
- Metrics to watch: p95 latency, mean token rejection rate, hallucination rate on a labeled subset, and token-per-inference.

Rollback and safety: feature-flag quant settings in the serving config, plus auto-fallback to baseline FP16 if quality regressions exceed threshold. We can instrument that during the pilot.

Happy to review a small run with your telemetry. If you can anonymize 500–1k prompt samples we'll run the eval and return a short report.

Kimberly Park
Applied ML — Inference Quality, Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick follow-ups from our engineering lead:

1) Our workload has a 30% long-tail: many one-off prompts that never repeat. Does Redwood still recommend cache-first for sessions where reuse is low?
2) For int4 experiments, do you gate on per-model artifacts? We need to know whether we can run int4 on a holdout cluster without impacting production.
3) On the commercial side, what flexibility exists for a mid-sized commit (around $300k ARR) if we want to stagger spend across two 6-month tranches?

If you can answer 1–3 succinctly we can fast-track internal approvals.

—Amit

Amit/Sana — answers below and next steps to keep momentum.

Short answers:
1) For 30% long-tail: prefer a hybrid approach — session KV cache for authenticated/repeat users + dynamic batching for one-off prompts. Cache-first provides win on the 70% repeat set and does not penalize one-offs if you keep adaptive batching enabled. We'll show you configuration that routes one-offs to a burst pool with higher per-token cost but guaranteed latency.
2) We absolutely support int4 experiments on dedicated holdout clusters. Our Private/Dedicated modes let you pin model variants and we can isolate int4 runs from prod traffic; auto-fallback preserves safety.
3) Commercial flexibility: yes — we can structure a $300k ARR commit as two 6-month tranches with an early-conversion discount and an earn-back credit if you convert to a 12-month commit. Ben will draft the formal term sheet.

Proposed immediate plan (mutual action plan):
- Week 1: FinOps provides anonymized 500-prompt eval set (Amit)
- Week 1–2: Redwood runs eval and returns quality delta and recommended quant profile (Kim)
- Week 2: Redwood provides pilot quote + conditional rebate language (Ben)
- Week 3: Procurement review and PO submission; onboarding kickoff if PO approved
